eyebrow: How each one proves who it is

steps.label: IAM user
steps.sub: password and/or access keys, valid indefinitely by default

steps.label: IAM role
steps.sub: no credentials of its own — assumed via sts:AssumeRole

steps.label: Temporary security credentials
steps.sub: access key, secret key, session token, minutes to hours to live

eyebrow: Trust policy: who can assume this role
caption: Trust policy answers "who can assume this role." The separate permissions policy answers "what can it do once assumed."

eyebrow: Workloads use roles, not embedded keys
code:
aws ec2 run-instances \
  --iam-instance-profile Name=AppServerRole \
  --image-id ami-0123456789abcdef0 \
  --instance-type t3.micro
caption: The instance profile assumes the role for the workload — credentials rotate themselves, nothing is stored on disk.
